items.title: Peter Ecklund interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998
items.q: I did play with him maybe eight or ten times a year and I played on one of his recordings

ctx.x: So a typical week for a trumpet player and cornet player, living in New York City, could be what? © Fiillius Jazz Archive -5-

Well I can tell you my weeks. Everyone, especially now because the music business is so fragmented, everyone really does different things it seems. Maybe I do more than most, but I think it’s not that atypical. Let’s see. Next week I return to New York on Monday and I play at a place called Michael’s Pub, operated by the original owner of Michael’s Pub, and it’s basically a scam, it’s a way of getting tourists who don’t realize that Woody Allen has moved on to another place, to come out and thinking that he might…
Yeah. Sure. Were you playing when Woody Allen was there?
